input.quote: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 is the only inspection right binding us: HDI may inspect the Company's payment-calculation records. Notice (30 days), timing (normal business hours) and cost (HDI bears all fees unconditionally, with no underpayment trigger) all meet or exceed the preferred position, and there is no remote or system-access language. However, the clause imposes no limit on frequency, so HDI could inspect repeatedly; unlimited audits fail the fallback (once per year) and sit in walk-away territory, so we propose the minimal insertion of a once-per-twelve-month cap. The inspector being HDI's General Manager rather than an independent auditor is a sub-element short of preferred only, and the records are in any event protected by the Section 8.3 confidentiality obligations, so we have not redlined that point.

ops.oldText: may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect
ops.newText: may, not more than once in any twelve (12) month period and upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a once-per-twelve-month cap on HDI's inspection right, since our playbook does not accept audits of unlimited frequency; the existing 30-day notice, business-hours and HDI-cost terms are unchanged.
proposal.summary: Cap HDI's record-inspection right at once per twelve months
